messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: high token usage alert for tenant FinEdge in dedicated pool df-pool-12 (us-west2-vpc). Spike detected at 12:03 UTC — token/sec 4x normal and billing spike. Please ack.

sarah: acked. i'm on it. getting logs from the pool now. FinEdge told success responses but their usage/charge doubled. confirmed alerts from quota service and billing-signal.

mike: thx. any idea if it's upstream (client) or our tokenizer/runtime?

sarah: initial grep in serving logs shows requests with huge token counts relative to payload size. example:
```
REQUEST id=abc123 tenant=finedge pool=df-pool-12
body_len=420 bytes text_preview="\u0046inEdge\n..."
reported_tokens=312
simple_estimate_by_len=45
```
looks like token_count is ~7x estimated by length. suspect encoding mismatch or double tokenization step. also seeing repeated header X-Client-Encoding missing.

alex: that screams UTF-16 being treated as UTF-8 in the tokenizer. if their client is sending UTF-16 LE, then every surrogate becomes extra bytes and BPE splits explode. can you paste the raw bytes for one request?

sarah: pasted below (hex snippet):
```
0000: 46 00 69 00 6e 00 45 00 64 00 67 00 65 00 0a 00 ...
```
that's "F\0i\0n\0E\0d\0g\0e\0\n\0" — yep UTF-16 LE.

mike: ok so client bug. why is our gateway not normalizing/declaring encoding? should have fallen back safely.

alex: our tokenizer expects UTF-8 bytes, we do not currently detect UTF-16. we rely on Content-Type + charset header. if header absent, runtime assumes utf-8. FinEdge client omitted charset and sent UTF-16 payload. bug.

priya: customer on support call says they didn't change anything last deploy. likely a library update in their stack toggled default encoding. we should contain the blast impact immediately — tenant isolation + billing mitigation.

sarah: mitigation plan proposal:
  1) temporary quota bump so customer requests are not throttled (preventing downstream retries) while we patch (billing flagged so charges are credited)
  2) route FinEdge traffic in gateway through tokenizer-shim that forces decode('utf-16-le') when raw bytes match BOM or 0x00 pattern
  3) mark the requests from this tenant as "billing-exempt" until corrected and open a billing incident
  4) patch tokenizer to auto-detect UTF-16 BOM or zero-byte patterns and decode before tokenization
  5) postmortem + customer comms

mike: agree. i'll do gateway route change and quota bump. running command now:
```
# set temporary quota override for tenant
rwctl quota override --tenant finedge --tokens-per-minute 500000 --expires 2025-10-01T14:00:00Z
```

mike: ran and verified in quota API. also added temporary routing rule:
```
rwctl gateway route add --tenant finedge --name force-decode-utf16 --match "pool:df-pool-12" --handler "tokenizer-shim://decode-utf16-if-bom"
```

alex: implementing shim in gateway now. small lua filter to detect NUL bytes and attempt UTF-16 LE decode before forwarding payload. patch going to canary groups 1/3 of nodes in df-pool-12.

sarah: canary logs look good. token counts drop to expected levels for canaryed requests. example after shim:
```
body_len=420 bytes text_preview="FinEdge\n..."
reported_tokens=48
```

tenant-support: looped in customer success and FinEdge dev lead via DM — asking them to confirm client-side fix. they said they can roll a patch within the hour.

billing-bot: billing alert: flagged 3 hours of overage for tenant finedge, estimated credit $1,800. manual review required. @billing-team please approve expedited credit.

mike: while we wait for client deploy, i'll expand the shim to full pool and set the shard rollout to 100%.

alex: rollout done to all df-pool-12 nodes. telemetry shows token/sec back to baseline and no downstream rate-limit errors.

sarah: sending a short exec/status to customer: "We've applied a temporary decode shim at the gateway to normalize UTF-16 payloads and waived any incidental overage while you deploy a client fix. Please deploy the patch to stop relying on the shim."

priya: customers asks for a short-term audit log showing affected requests (start/stop) and token counts for reconciliation.

sarah: generated CSV and uploaded to internal bucket: s3://redwood-incident-exports/finedge/1753216789-token-audit.csv — shared with tenant-support and billing.

mike: follow-ups:
  - eng-runtime to implement auto-detect/decode in tokenizer (alex owning)
  - infra to add a warning metric for requests with NUL bytes in first 200 bytes (mike owning)
  - billing to reconcile charges and apply credit (billing team owning)
  - cs to coordinate customer comms and confirm client patch (tenant-support owning)

alex: I'll open PR for tokenizer auto-detect. quick patch: look for UTF-16 BOM (FF FE / FE FF) or >15% zero bytes in first 256 bytes then decode as utf-16-le/utf-16-be accordingly. tests added.

sarah: incident severity: S2 (customer-impacting but mitigated). tagging for postmortem. thanks all.

incident-bot: incident acknowledged and handed off to oncall for postmortem follow-up. runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/tokenizer-encoding-mismatch

mike: closing alert. will keep thread open for postmortem notes.

sarah: I'll post timeline and writeup in incidents/postmortems once PR and billing resolved.

tenant-support: FinEdge confirmed client patch deployed at 13:08 UTC and validated token counts back to normal on their side. asked for official incident summary. noted appreciation for quick mitigation :thumbsup:

sarah: thanks team. actions recorded in JIRA INC-5942. end of thread.
